stem_book: If the roots of 1/(x + p) + 1/(x + q) = 1/r are equal in magnitude but opposite in sign, then p + q = 2r and the product of the roots is k(p² + q²). Then k = (a) −1 (b) −1/2 (c) −3/2 (d) −2
reason: Print's garbled 'show that p + q = 2r the product of roots is' rewritten as a single clear question.
work: x² + (p + q − 2r)x + pq − r(p + q) = 0; sum 0 ⇒ r = (p+q)/2 ⇒ product = pq − (p+q)²/2 = −(p² + q²)/2 ⇒ k = −1/2
